title: cuscuta planiflora subsp. papillosa
intro: Cuscuta planiflora subsp. papillosa, commonly known as Dodder, is a parasitic plant that derives its nutrients by connecting itself to the vascular system of its host plant. This plant has been traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties, offering several health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immune-boosting effects. The therapeutic actions of Cuscuta planiflora subsp. papillosa include its ability to reduce fever, alleviate pain, and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic actions include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds, which have been shown to possess anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer properties.
